To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the computed-torque scheme is a superior controller for trajectory tracking of the DD Arm II, as long as there are no actuator saturations.

1) The computed-torque controller outperforms the decoupled joint control scheme, 2) the performance of the decoupled control scheme can be improved by increasing the control gains and 3) the performance of both schemes is limited by the torque saturation of the actuators.

the performance of the independent joint controller is very sensitive to the choice of the controller gains, and the computed-torque controller outperforms the joint controller as long as there are not torque saturation in actuators.
